$comment: How a test project is split across CI jobs, the same on every OS (#2054); read by .github/scripts/test-shard-filter.ps1. Each project's 'shards' lists the class-name prefixes of every shard but the last; the last shard is everything the others did not take, so a new class always runs somewhere. A prefix matches by contains on FullyQualifiedName, and a shard leaves out what an earlier shard took, so the shards never overlap: a class named in an earlier shard is out of a later one's family prefix (StarInjection before Star, ViewerWaveletDerive before Viewer, PlanetarySharpening before Planetary). The workflow's matrices state the shard count beside this file, and the script refuses a count that disagrees with it. Balanced on two things, from the per-class times of run 42885521250 (tools/ci-test-timings.py; ByArea, the shared planetary render and the one 61 s timeout taken off): each shard's summed time, which four test threads share, and its longest CHAIN, since xUnit runs a collection's classes (and a class's tests) one after another, so a shard is never shorter than its longest chain however few its other tests. Round 3 put the five planetary viewer classes (one collection, 324 s on Linux) in one shard and that shard took 6 minutes; here ViewerWaveletDerive sits apart from the rest of that collection, as do the functional suite's Session and NodeProcesses chains, which two shards could not split below 5 minutes on Windows. Unit 4 shards: summed 800, 869, 720, 780 s on Linux x64 and 791, 723, 799, 800 on Windows, chains at most 215 s. Functional 3: summed 378, 424, 308 on Linux and 481, 506, 378 on Windows, chains at most 208. That is 18 test jobs a run (4 unit shards on each of three runners, 3 functional on each of two), against the org plan's 20 jobs at once; rebalance from that table on the PR that changes it.
